heard: Enigma had one flaw, a letter never came out as itself. Not brute force. 159 billion billion settings. At a million a second, that's 5 million years. Your job at Bletchley Park, 1940, find today's settings. First, guess a phrase. Units kept sending nothing to report. In German, that's 25 letters. Slide it under the message. Wherever a letter lands on itself, that spot is impossible. Here, two spots crash. Four are left. But a spot isn't the key. Each letter pair under it is a clue. Turing's bones spun through all 17 ,576 rotor positions and stopped only where every clue fit. About 20 minutes per rotor order. Five million years became a day's work. All because a letter could never be itself. Subscribe if you'd have tried every setting.
